body:
Source: GitHub issue #822 (release-audit class false-green, P1-high, security). Re-verified on main @ e2bc60ab: `plugins/adlc-gemini/rails-checker.mjs`'s `checkRail` builds match candidates via `canonicalizePath` (lexical, no case normalization) and `resolveRailPath` (symlink-aware `realpathSync`, around line 138-160: for an EXISTING path it realpaths the whole thing, but for a NOT-YET-EXISTING path — the common case for a `write` creating a new file — it realpaths only the deepest EXISTING ancestor and re-appends the not-yet-existing TAIL VERBATIM, uncased). Neither candidate is ever compared case-insensitively. On a case-insensitive filesystem (default macOS APFS, default Windows NTFS), writing `src/frozen.js` when the frozen rail is declared as `src/FROZEN.js` creates/edits the SAME on-disk file as far as the OS is concerned, but `checkRail`'s exact-string / `globMatch` comparison (via `plugins/adlc-gemini/generated-glob-match.mjs`) never matches it — the write is silently ALLOWED. `.adlc/tickets.json` vs `.adlc/TICKETS.json` is the trust-root-relevant instance of the same class. On Linux (case-sensitive), `src/FROZEN.js` and `src/frozen.js` are genuinely different files and must NOT be conflated — a blanket case-fold would be a NEW bug (over-denial of legitimately distinct files) on that platform, so the fix must be filesystem-case-sensitivity AWARE, not a blind lowercase-everything change.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. `plugins/adlc-gemini/rails-checker.mjs`: `checkRail({filePath, tool, root, env})` (the exported deny/allow decision), `railPreconditions` (resolves the active ticket's frozen rails), `canonicalizePath`, `resolveRailPath` (both exported, pure-ish path helpers), `classifyTool`. `globMatch` is imported from `./generated-glob-match.mjs` (a generated verbatim copy — do not hand-edit it; if glob matching itself needs a case-insensitive mode, add a NEW comparison path in rails-checker.mjs rather than modifying the generated file). No case-sensitivity probe exists anywhere in this repo yet — this ticket introduces the first one, scoped to this plugin (it ships zero-dependency and inlines its own helpers, per the file's existing style — do not add a cross-plugin shared dependency).

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. Add a pure, injectable case-sensitivity PROBE: given a directory that is known to exist (e.g. `root`), determine whether the filesystem there is case-insensitive. A safe, side-effect-free method: stat a file/directory known to exist under `root` (e.g. `root` itself, or `.adlc` if present) with its case FLIPPED (e.g. uppercase the whole leaf segment) via `existsSync`/`statSync`, and check whether it resolves to the SAME inode/real path as the original-case spelling (compare `realpathSync` results, or `fs.statSync(...).ino` where available) — never write anything to disk to test this (a probe that CREATES a temp file to test case-folding is more invasive and slower than necessary and risks polluting the ticket-store directory; prefer statting something that already exists). Cache the result per `root` (mirroring the existing `cache` pattern in `plugins/adlc-herdr/lib/repo-root.mjs` if useful as a style reference — but this stays self-contained, no cross-plugin import). Make the probe function itself exported and independently unit-testable, and accept an injectable `stat`/`existsSync` for deterministic tests that don't depend on the CI runner's actual filesystem.
2. In `checkRail`, when the probe reports case-insensitive for `root`: in ADDITION to the existing exact-case candidates, also build a case-FOLDED (lowercased) candidate and compare it against a case-folded copy of every declared rail glob. A case-insensitive match on an insensitive filesystem → DENY (this only ever WIDENS denial, never narrows it — the exact-case path stays as the primary, always-checked signal). On a case-SENSITIVE filesystem (the probe says so, or the probe result is unknown/probe failed), behavior is BYTE-IDENTICAL to today — no case-folded comparison at all, so `src/FROZEN.js` (rail) and `src/frozen.js` (unrelated file) on Linux remain correctly distinguished.
3. Apply the same case-insensitive-aware comparison to the not-yet-existing-tail case in `resolveRailPath`'s candidate (or handle it directly in `checkRail`'s candidate set) — the write-creating-a-new-file path is the one the issue's `.adlc/TICKETS.json` example concerns.
4. Fail-closed convention preserved: if the probe itself throws or can't determine sensitivity, treat as case-SENSITIVE (i.e., do NOT add the extra denial-widening comparison) rather than guessing — this matches the file's existing 'fail closed on the things that must never be silently allowed, but never invent surprising new denials from an uncertain signal' balance (contrast with `railPreconditions`'s own fail-closed-on-malformed-input pattern, which is about the RAIL DECLARATION being untrustworthy, not about filesystem uncertainty — do not conflate the two).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 The case-sensitivity probe function, tested directly with injected mocks: reports insensitive when a flipped-case stat resolves to the same real path as the original, sensitive when it does not (or the flipped-case path does not exist at all), and sensitive (not insensitive) when the probe's underlying calls throw. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-gemini/test/case-sensitivity.test.mjs`
- AC2 `checkRail` with an INJECTED case-insensitive probe result: a write to `src/frozen.js` is DENIED when the active ticket's rail is declared `src/FROZEN.js` (and vice versa, mixed case both directions), for both an EXISTING frozen file and a NOT-YET-EXISTING new file at the differently-cased path. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-gemini/test/case-sensitivity.test.mjs`
- AC3 `checkRail` with an INJECTED case-SENSITIVE probe result: `src/frozen.js` (unrelated file) is still ALLOWED when the rail is `src/FROZEN.js` — no behavior change on a case-sensitive filesystem, regression-pinned against the current test suite's existing case-matched-only assertions. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-gemini/test/case-sensitivity.test.mjs` and the existing `plugins/adlc-gemini/test/*.test.mjs` suite unmodified in its case-sensitive assertions
- AC4 `.adlc/TICKETS.json` (or any case variant of the ticket-store trust root) is denied on an injected case-insensitive filesystem, matching the issue's specific trust-root example. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-gemini/test/case-sensitivity.test.mjs`
- AC5 Existing suite green (confirm actual baseline count; no existing test should need to change — this is purely additive). verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-gemini/test/*.test.mjs`
- AC6 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: modifying `generated-glob-match.mjs` (a generated file — never hand-edit); any other plugin's rails-checker (each is a separate, non-shared inlined copy per this repo's zero-dependency plugin convention).

PROCESS (ADLC). Work only in your assigned worktree. P3: the rails on this ticket are frozen — if the fix appears to require editing a rail path, STOP and report; never set ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS. P4: TDD — write test/case-sensitivity.test.mjs first, run it RED, then implement. P5 before opening the PR: the package suite, `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` (exit 0), then the cross-model review loop (see lane instructions) until a round is clean. Do not add gate-manifest entries. Keep the diff to plugins/adlc-gemini/rails-checker.mjs, its test, and this ticket's shard. PR title `fix(adlc-gemini): ...`, body must contain `Closes #822`.
title: plugin(adlc-gemini): detect case-insensitive filesystems and deny a differently-cased rail-path write, fail closed
